hunts.label: Saturday, Nov 7
hunts.subtitle: A thin moon, a cool clear morning, and bucks with their minds on something else.

rules.title: Saturday checklist (the clocks already changed on Nov 1)
items: **Hunter orange** on, hat and vest (required Oct 17 to Jan 1 for firearm hunters).
**Real hunting is legal light, 6:05 am, to about 9:00 am.** Be unloaded and out by 9:00.

**Dove season reopens today** and **Coastal ducks reopen today.** Both are opportunity only. You need your HIP number and a 3-shell plug in the gun for any migratory bird. Ducks also need the federal duck stamp, the state waterfowl privilege and steel shot only.
**Crow is open on Saturdays.** HIP and plug apply.
rules.note: Confirm seasons, bag limits and shooting hours in the NCWRC Regulations Digest. Check your phone and watch both show the post-change time.

conditions.source: Source: hourly point forecast from a commercial weather service (the National Weather Service page was out of date for this day). Sun and moon times from a published sun table.
items: **Walk-in, 4:55 am:** about 55°F. Light northwest breeze, 3 to 4 mph. Partly cloudy. Humidity near 97 to 99%, so wet leaves and dew.
**9 am:** about 56°F. North-northwest wind near 8 mph. Mostly sunny.
**Precipitation:** 11% or less all morning. Dry. Afternoon high near 64°F.
**Moon:** waning crescent, only about 7% lit. It rose near 3:57 am, so a sliver is up low in the east on the walk-in. New moon is Monday.
conditions.meaning: **What it likely means (my assumption, not proven):** a warm, damp start turning clear and breezy. Deer often move best right at first light, then feed or chase until the wind builds past 7 mph. A dark moon can mean more daylight movement. Wet leaves keep your steps quiet, and the rising breeze covers small sounds after 7.
conditions.hours_note: No gust figures were listed. Coldest point is about 7 am. Wind builds from 3 to 8 mph through the morning, so expect the thread to lean harder after 8.

wind.label: from the north-northwest, 3 mph at the walk-in rising to 8 mph by 9 am

in_season: **Deer, either sex** (gun season, day 22). Seeking phase: bucks are on their feet and checking does.

in_season.text: **Dove** (second segment Nov 7 to Nov 28, 15 a day). Opportunity only.
in_season.tip: Needs HIP and a 3-shell plug. Use #7.5 and shoot only birds crossing to the north, never low and never toward the house or field.

in_season.text: **Coastal-zone ducks** reopen today (Nov 7 to 28). Skip unless you have steel shot.
in_season.tip: Needs HIP, federal duck stamp, state waterfowl privilege, steel shot and a 3-shell plug. Wood ducks may leave the swamp at first light. No steel, no ducks. Never carry lead shot while duck hunting.

in_season: **Crow** (Saturday is an open day) and **snipe** (open to Feb 27): opportunity only with HIP and plug.
Closed: woodcock (opens Dec 10). Quail opens Nov 21. Turkey is a spring season.

in_season.tip: Bobcat is open. Bear opens next Saturday, Nov 14. You are not hunting either. Slugs stay zipped, for defense only.

plan.title: The plan: the Back Door Seat, wind in your face in the tall pines
plan.why: **Why here:** the main trail runs NE through the tall pines to the Junction. Pick the stretch about 60 yards before the Junction. Step 20 yards EAST of the trail and sit against the widest pine, facing N and NW. With the wind from the NNW, it blows into your face. Your scent goes SSE, behind you, away from the swamp corridor and the trail. Deer using the trail or swamp edge come from the north and west, into the wind. **Caution:** a deer that comes up from the pasture side would smell you. Watch your south side by turning your head, never the gun. **Timing:** legal light is 6:05, so be seated by 5:20, about 45 minutes before. Leave the yard at 4:55. This is new ground, and it also teaches you how the pines hold the wind.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail, heading NE through the pines. Red light low. Three steps, listen, three steps. Count your steps.
At the tallest pines, about 60 yards short of the Junction, leave the trail to the EAST. Walk 20 yards in and pick a trunk wider than your shoulders.
Sit with your back to the trunk. Face N and NW. Check what is behind every lane. No house, no field, nothing south, southwest or southeast.
Load at the sit, muzzle pointing N. Safety on. Tie a 12-inch thread to the barrel. If it points toward the trail corridor instead of SSE, slide 20 yards and sit again.
Legal light. Scan in sectors, left to right. The first 30 minutes of light is your best window.
No deer? Stay put. With a dark moon and wind rising to 6 mph, a buck may still come through. Keep scanning with your eyes, not your head.
Swap 00 for #4. Walk the loop trail east and south, slow, into the wind. Squirrel and rabbit. Shoot N, NW, NE, E or W only.
Walk your drag route from the sit back toward the yard. Count the steps.
Unloaded and out at the yard edge. Log what you saw with a "note:" message.

items: **In the gun:** 00 buckshot in the magazine. Modified choke. Safety on. Plug in.
**Right pocket:** #4 and #7.5 birdshot. Swap in at about 8:30.
**Also carry:** knife, hatchet, gloves, 12-inch thread, 10 feet of cord, dry layer.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot.
Never shoot buckshot or slugs without the ground behind the target.
Keep buckshot and birdshot in different pockets. Check by feel.
Steel only for ducks. Do not carry lead shot while duck hunting.

animals.name: Deer
paragraphs: **Local:** common. They bed in the swamp thickets and travel the swamp edge and the pines.
**Today:** seeking phase, dark moon, mild, wind in your face. Best window (assumption): 6:05 to 7:30, then a second chance after the wind settles.
**Shot:** broadside or quartering away only. 30 yards maximum with 00. Aim behind the front shoulder, middle of the body. Shoot only N, NW, NE, E or W. Never south.

details.title: Technique: head down means move, head up means freeze
steps: A deer that is feeding or sniffing has its head down. That is your moment to move a hand or shift your weight, slowly.
When the head comes up, stop everything. Do not blink if you can help it. Wait it out.
If it stares at you for more than a minute, stay frozen. It will often drop its head and go on.
Before you raise the gun, check three things: broadside or quartering away, ground behind it, and the shot is N, NW, NE, E or W.
details.note: A deer will only spook once. Raise the gun only when the head is down or behind a tree.

after: **Tip:** count to three before you squeeze. In that count, check the backstop and your arc. It costs nothing and stops mistakes.
**Tip:** a warm morning in the mid 50s means meat spoils fast. If you take a deer, get it gutted, opened up and cooled within the hour.

animals.name: Squirrel
paragraphs: **Local:** gray squirrels are seen often. Fox squirrel is possible.
**Today:** a warm, dry morning, so they feed early. The rising breeze after 8 hides your steps. (Assumption.)
**Shot:** head and neck. #4 to 30 yards. #7.5 to 25 yards. Only with a trunk or the ground behind it.

details.title: Technique: find the leaf nest, then wait nearby
steps: Look up into the forks of the tall trees. A round ball of leaves is a squirrel nest.
Walk to a spot about 25 yards away, behind a trunk, and sit down.
Wait 15 minutes. A squirrel leaves its nest to feed and comes back to it.
Shoot when the head shows and there is a trunk or the ground behind it.

after: **Tip:** a squirrel in a nest tree often goes quiet if it saw you. Move slowly and sit; give it time.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: **Local:** likely at the feed bins and along thick edges of the loop.
**Today:** wind-up mornings keep them in cover, because they cannot hear well. Walk into the wind.
**Shot:** #4 to 30 yards, N, NW, NE, E or W only.

details.title: Technique: walk into the wind along the thick edge
steps: Pick an edge of briars or thick brush near the loop.
Walk it slowly with the wind in your face, so the rabbit hears and smells you late.
Hold still when you pass a thick patch. A rabbit hiding close will often break at your third or fourth step.
Check where you would shoot before you take the next step. If the rabbit runs south, let it go.

after: **Safety:** wear gloves when you handle it. Check the liver for white spots.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Opportunity only. A raccoon heading to a den near the swamp or bins at dawn is possible.
**Look for:** a raccoon track in mud looks like a tiny hand with five long fingers. Check the mud near the beaver lodge.
**Shot:** #4, head and neck, 20 yards, with a trunk or the ground behind. Never toward the house or field.

animals.name: Dove and crow (opportunity)
paragraphs: **Dove:** season reopens today. Doves feed in open fields, so the pasture side gets most of the traffic, and that is off your land. A passing bird over the pines is a bonus, not a plan.
**Crow:** open on Saturdays. If a flock goes over, take it only with a clear northern sky. #7.5, plug in, HIP on you.
**Rule:** both need the 3-shell plug and HIP. Doves are small, so #7.5 at 25 yards.

details.title: Technique: shoot the flight line, not the bird
steps: Watch which way a dove flies for a few seconds before you decide.
Mount the gun early and swing through the bird, then keep swinging.
Never shoot at a low bird or at one toward the house or field. Sky shots to the north only.

skill.title: Skill of the week: set up a sit near a scrape line
skill.principle: **Core principle:** you already know how to tell a fresh scrape from an old one. Now use it. Deer visit scrapes at the edges of the day. Do not sit on the scrape. Sit downwind of it, with a lane you can see.

sections.title: Choose the sit (do this on the walk out)
steps: 1. Find a scrape: a patch of bare dirt pawed clean, under a low branch that is chewed or broken.
2. Stand on it and note where the wind would carry your scent. Today that is SSE.
3. Pick a tree 25 to 30 yards on the DOWNWIND side of the scrape, so deer coming to the scrape do not cross your scent.
4. Check the backstop: nothing south, no house or field behind a shot line.
5. Cut nothing. Break no branches. Leave the area as you found it.

sections.title: Approach and entry (the part that is easy to get wrong)
steps: 1. Walk in from the downwind side, never across the scrape.
2. Touch nothing near the scrape. Your scent is the problem.
3. Arrive in the dark, 45 minutes before legal light.
4. Leave the same way, after the hunt is done.

details.title: Tap to open: why not sit right at the scrape
paragraphs: A buck checks a scrape by working the air downwind of it. If you sit there, he smells you before he steps in. Sit to the side and downwind of the scrape and his nose is looking the wrong way.

skill.checkpoint: **Checkpoint:** if you find a fresh scrape, count the steps from the yard to it and describe the tree you would sit in. Send it in a "note:" message.

land.intro: Today you learn how the wind moves through the pines. Make notes on the walk out.
steps: Count your steps from the yard to the Back Door Seat, and from the seat to the Junction.
Run the thread test at 5:25 and 8:00. Write down which way it points each time.
Walk the pines and look for scrapes or rubs. Note any fresh bare dirt and the tree closest to it.
Look for a deer trail within 100 yards of your sit. Note which way it runs and how wide it is.
Send a "note:" message with what you found. Next week's plan will use it.

safety: **Shooting arc:** north, northwest and northeast. Never beyond east or west. NEVER south. The house is SW, the field is SE, the neighbor is south.
Buckshot and slugs need the ground behind them.
Hunter orange on, hat and vest. Real hunting ends about 9:00. Be unloaded and out.
Mild and damp at dawn, about 55°F, but wet leaves and roots are slick. Walk slowly with the red light, and watch for holes and stumps.
Warm weather: if you take a deer, cool the meat within the hour. Do not leave it in the sun.
Bear and fox are in the area. Slugs are for defense only.
hunts.regs: Check the NCWRC Regulations Digest for season dates, deer reporting, bag limits and migratory bird requirements.
hunts.gaps: No hunting entries in your Daily Notes this week. The National Weather Service page was out of date, so the hourly table came from another forecast service with no issue time and no gust figures. Moon illumination ranged from 3 to 8% across sources, and moonrise differed by about an hour between them; I used the value two sources agreed on. The Digest was not checked directly for the crow day rule; crow dates came from a secondary source.
